We then use misaligned prompts asking the model to “Describe the N + k N+k [objects] in the image,”, where k ∈ { 1 , 2 , … , 5 } k\in\{1,2,\ldots,5\} denotes the discrepancy distance between the prompt and the visual input. A PIH occurs when the model proceeds to describe N + k N+k objects without correcting the count, despite contradictory visual evidence. See Appendix ˜ A for additional details. Figure 2 shows the proportion of outputs that either match the prompted count ( N + k N+k , blue curves) or the true count ( N N , orange curves) across a range of object quantities and prompt offsets ( k k ). The x x -axis denotes the true number of objects ( N N ), and the y y -axis shows the fraction of responses aligned with either the prompt or ground truth. We observe a consistent pattern across all three models. For images containing small numbers of objects ( 2 2 - 4 4 objects), models typically resist misleading prompts and report the true count, demonstrated by the orange curves being mostly higher than the blue curves.
